clue.text: One poem filled empty day after sun set

indicators.note: the emptied word for day is stuffed with the poem, so one piece sits inside the other
the one and filled pieces are placed behind the star word, so it comes first

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the Roman numeral for one
day with its middle emptied out leaves its first and last letters
If is Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A writer fills a blank day with a single poem after the sun goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like it describes the sun setting, but it is the definition, as concrete sets. SOL + I + D(IF)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly or concrete that has set has hardened into a firm state, which is exactly what solidify means as a verb.

clue.text: Number penned by Gilbert & Sullivan, uplifting composition

indicators.note: something penned by others is enclosed between them
in a down entry lifting up means reading from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: initial of Gilbert
No. is the abbreviation for number
initial of Sullivan

explanation.surface: A cheerful number written by the operetta duo Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like the definition, a musical number, but it is the abbreviation; the definition is 'composition'.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is a short musical composition with words for singing, the kind of piece a songwriter produces.

clue.text: Flier poet drops in

indicators.note: dropping something means leaving it out, so the following little word is removed

parts.note: Philip Larkin, the English poet
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A bird-loving poet pays a casual visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops in' reads as a phrasal verb for visiting, but drops is the removal signal and in is what goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird famous for singing as it rises high in the air, so it is a flier.

clue.text: Club where loon punched by plonker at the back

indicators.note: a punch makes a hole and goes in, so one letter is struck into the bird word

parts.note: the loon is the American name for the bird the British call a diver

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of plonker

explanation.surface: A nightclub scene where a lunatic gets thumped by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Loon and plonker both look like insults; a loon is a diving bird, and plonker (British slang for a fool) just gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the driver is the club with the largest head, used for long shots off the tee.

clue.text: Sucker digging weeds?

parts.note: surface reading: a gullible gardener who enjoys pulling out unwanted plants
setter's reading: weeds are clothes, as in widow's weeds, and digging is slang for liking, so a dupe who is keen on clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Weeds is an old word for garments and to dig something is to like it, so a sucker for clothes is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone duped by every passing trend in clothing, wearing it however unflattering, is mocked as a slave to style.

clue.text: West-facing complex of temples briefly visited by old trainspotter

indicators.note: in an across entry facing west means reading right to left, backwards
a visitor goes inside, so the old abbreviation is placed within
cut short, so the last letter of the temple complex's name is dropped

parts.note: Karnak is the great temple complex at Luxor in Egypt
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An elderly trainspotter tours an Egyptian temple site, oddly facing west.
explanation.walkthrough: Karnak, at Luxor, is Egypt's great temple complex; 'briefly' trims it before it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorak is British slang for an obsessive hobbyist, named after the hooded coat stereotypically worn by people logging trains on platforms.

clue.text: Winner primarily missing in person who fails — one of those?

definitions.text: Winner primarily missing in person who fails — one of those?

indicators.note: a failing structure collapses, so the remaining letters fall into a new order
something missing in a phrase is absent from it, so that letter is taken out
primarily means first, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: opening letter of winner
taken as written

explanation.surface: With no winner in sight, the clue wonders whether a person who keeps failing belongs among the hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone lacking a winner, a failure, is one of the hopeless cases.
explanation.definitionFit: No-hopers are people or horses with no chance of success, so a person who fails, minus any winning streak, counts among them.

clue.text: Removing leader in bully, house stops Trump

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so these pieces go into the middle of the card word

parts.note: in card games to ruff is to play a trump

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: opening letter of bully
house, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo

explanation.surface: Political satire: a bully in the White House blocks Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump and house suggest American politics; trump is the card term and house is the bingo game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing off means wiping or scraping away a mark, so the phrase describes removing something from a surface.

clue.text: Fictional poison pretty OK in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A reader judges a toxin in a novel to be pretty okay.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes 'in', so 'novel' alone is the anagram signal; the surface reads 'in novel' as where the poison appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Kryptonite is the invented mineral from Superman's home planet that weakens him, a made-up toxin from comics.

clue.text: Rainbow is beginning to shine in reflection of light source — bulb!

indicators.note: the rainbow and following pieces sit inside the mirrored light source
a reflection shows things mirrored, so the source word reads backwards

parts.note: the sun is our main source of light
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of shine
a rainbow is an arc of colour in the sky

explanation.surface: A rainbow begins to glow in reflected sunlight, and a light bulb finishes the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' seems to continue the light-source theme, but it is a plant bulb; the myth of Narcissus and his reflection adds a neat echo.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcissus is a spring flower, including daffodils, that grows from an underground bulb, so the plant is named by its storage organ.

clue.text: Tricky device, needle-like drill

parts.note: a needle is sharp
drill means repeated practice

explanation.surface: Describes a pointed boring tool as an ingenious gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Device and drill suggest a workshop tool; device means a scheme and drill means practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest or underhand dealing, a crafty scheme that is just short of illegal.

clue.text: Better half's other half, central?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wife's spouse, since she is the better half
second meaning, whimsical: like a hub, at the middle of things

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a playful coinage: something hub-like would be at the centre, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubby is a fond informal word for husband, the spouse of a woman whose partner calls her his better half.

clue.text: Mark, cryptically intense?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dot printed in a number
second meaning: read cryptically, intense splits as in tens, which is what base ten counting means

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'intense' as 'in tens': a decimal system works in tens, and the dot is its key symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal point is the dot that separates whole units from tenths, the mark at the heart of counting in tens.

clue.text: Player in pursuit of American vehicles?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American comic actor of Caddyshack and National Lampoon films
second meaning, whimsical: a hunt after Chevrolets, popularly called Chevys

explanation.walkthrough: Player means an actor here. Chevy is the nickname for a Chevrolet car, so chasing them would be a Chevy chase.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian took his stage name from the old ballad Chevy Chase, and the phrase also reads as chasing Chevrolet cars.

clue.text: Rough tongue picked up something alcoholic

parts.note: hard and rough both mean harsh

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio, meaning heard, so the sound of the word matters

parts.note: a tongue is a licker

explanation.surface: Someone with a coarse palate tastes strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The tongue is the organ that licks, so it is a licker.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard liquor is strong distilled spirit such as whisky or vodka, as opposed to beer or wine.

clue.text: A bargain when cap removed, great deal

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so taking it off drops the first letter

parts.note: something that is a bargain is cheap

explanation.surface: A shopper notes that a bargain becomes an even better deal once the price cap is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAP without its first letter. 'Great deal' sounds like a bargain, but it means a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of something, informally, is a lot of it, as in heaps of time, a large quantity.

clue.text: Plant seed covering trail on surface

indicators.note: the word for seed wraps around the other pieces like a cover

parts.note: seed in the biblical sense of offspring

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another is placed after it

parts.note: nap is the raised surface of a fabric
to drag is to trail along behind

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a seed coat and a trailing stem across the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening words mislead: seed means a son, and surface is the nap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower whose blooms open like jaws when squeezed.

clue.text: One Direction welcoming drunk in, OK being most squiffy?

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the direction holds the other letters

parts.note: west is one of the compass directions

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy band welcomes a drunk fan, who is fine despite being tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is the boy band in the surface; read it as one compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy means slightly drunk but also askew, and wonky means crooked or unsteady, so the most lopsided is wonkiest.

clue.text: I've day without a radio broadcast for onscreen recording of thoughts

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
going without something means it is left out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spends a day with no radio, wanting a record of their musings on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from I'VE DAY to leave IVEDY, then add RADIO and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A video diary is a series of filmed personal reflections, the camera version of a written journal.

clue.text: What might reveal a little of thief, I think?

definitions.text: What might reveal a little of thief, I think?

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of thief, the I and the start of think

explanation.surface: A detective muses that an image might show a bit of what the thief looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an e-fit reveals a little of a thief's face, and the answer sits inside 'thief, I think'.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-fit is a computer-built facial composite made from witness descriptions, showing police roughly what a suspect looks like.

clue.text: Love dressing king in what would suit knight?

indicators.note: dressing someone means putting clothes around them, so the love word wraps the king

parts.note: amour is French for love
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A romance fit for a medieval court, with a lover clothing the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval knight wore a metal suit of plate mail into battle, and suit puns on clothing.

clue.text: Heart-breaking condition caught, result of a combination of knocks?

definitions.text: result of a combination of knocks?

indicators.note: breaking in after the other parts, so that the central part is attached at the end

parts.note: c is the scorecard abbreviation for caught
rickets is a bone-softening disease
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: A medical report on a heart condition picked up after a series of blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks' sounds like injuries, but in cricket a knock is a batsman's innings, and the total of all the innings is the team's score.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket score is the total runs a side makes, built up from the individual innings that cricketers informally call knocks.

clue.text: Tense — as lips?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nervous and on edge
second meaning, whimsical: lips are edges, as of a cup, so lips are edge-like

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar, but it means nervous; a lip is the rim of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy describes someone nervy and on edge, while the playful second sense means having the nature of a rim or brim.

clue.text: Said right, introduction not needed

indicators.note: with no introduction the word starts without its first letter

parts.note: morally right, ethical

explanation.surface: Someone said the right thing, no introduction needed.
explanation.walkthrough: MORAL loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral agreement or exam is spoken rather than written, so oral means said out in speech.

clue.text: A pretty oblique mark

parts.note: taken as written
cute means pretty or sweet

explanation.surface: A teacher scrawls a rather slanting tick in the margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pretty oblique mark' reads as a rather slanted grade, but pretty is the adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute accent is the slanting stroke over a vowel, as in café, a diagonal diacritic.

clue.text: Purchasing system brotherhood discussed?

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a brotherhood is an order of men, such as monks

explanation.surface: A committee debates a monastery's way of buying supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is a way of buying goods from a catalogue, with orders sent and goods delivered by post.

clue.text: A seaman concerned with reversing mistakes

indicators.note: reversing turns the string of letters around so it reads from the end

parts.note: taken as written
tar is an old word for a sailor
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A sailor is worried about backing his vessel into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural used for a list of printing errors, so it means mistakes.

clue.text: Scuffle in breach of contract in settlement of others' costs

indicators.note: a breach is a break into something, so the fight bursts into the other word

parts.note: a deal is an agreement or contract
a fray is a fight or scuffle

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out over a broken contract, with lawyers' bills to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'breach of contract' look like one phrase, but 'in breach of' is the insertion signal and 'contract' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray is to pay someone's expenses, so defrayal is the act of meeting those charges on their behalf.
